title: Finite-operation realization data on normalized finite-Tor coefficient systems
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$ and finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its recorded integer ring $R$, uniformizer $\varpi$ and quotients $A_{n+1}=R/\varpi^{n+1}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with compactification $c=(j,p)$ [def-nagata-compactification]. Use the ordinary derived categories of strict semilinear coefficient systems, their exact evaluations, actual quotient transitions, tensor/internal Hom and simultaneous resolution models [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Define $\mathscr N_W$ as the full subcategory of normalized systems [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] whose every level belongs to the finite-Tor constructible category [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]; no bound common to the levels is imposed.

A finite-operation realization datum consists of an exact open extension left adjoint to the actual sequence-site inverse image, a universal right-derived proper image with its normalized adjunction and K-flat tensor comparison, functors $F:\mathscr N_X\to\mathscr N_Y$ and $G:\mathscr N_Y\to\mathscr N_X$, an adjunction $F\dashv G$, and an identification of $F$ with this proper/open composite on all derived arrows. It includes evaluation isomorphisms to the finite operations $F_n,G_n$ of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional], equations identifying their units and counits, and, for every $n\le m$, the two quotient-transition equations: the transition of $F(M)$ is $q_{m,n}$ followed by $F_n$ of the input transition, and that of $G(N)$ is $b_{m,n}$ followed by $G_n$ of the input transition, under the evaluation isomorphisms. Here $q$ and its adjunction mate $b$ are those of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional], and each input transition is the adjoint of the actual system restriction map under quotient tensor/restriction adjunction.

For such data define the system projection using the geometric counit, inverse open-unit tensor comparison and canonical pullback compositor. Define the internal enriched arrow $f_*\mathcal I_X(M,GN)\to\mathcal I_Y(FM,N)$ as the tensor-Hom transpose of the left-oriented projection followed by geometric counit, evaluation and exceptional counit. An ordinary/direct-image sections comparison is normalized by restriction from the terminal site object; its derived comparison is normalized by the corresponding universal derived units on every cochain complex. Whenever the internal enriched arrow is invertible, define the global mapping-system arrow by derived sections of its inverse followed by that derived sections comparison. These are definitions of actual derived-system maps; no existence or invertibility of a realization datum or of an enriched arrow is asserted by this definition. The actual sequence pullback and its canonical compositor are those of [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]; the simultaneous section tensor model is [def-coef-semilinear-system-models], universal geometric derivation and cochain adjunction normalization are [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison], and exact open localization uses [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization].

The proper and open finite evaluations are those of [def-sf-integral-system-operations]. Identify the ordinary geometric direct image with its published presentation by the identity on every underlying section; the left-adjoint uniqueness comparison and exact localization transport the canonical inverse-image evaluation of [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison]. The proper comparison is right-adjoint uniqueness relative to this fixed inverse-image transport, and the open comparison is left-adjoint uniqueness relative to it. The support evaluation is their composite followed by the published proper and open evaluation comparisons; the evaluation isomorphism for F is required to equal the evaluation of its support identification followed by this composite. Include invertibility of the displayed open-unit tensor arrow and the equalities identifying canonical quotient restriction in the two finite presentations, for X and Y, as proof data of a realization. These are requirements on a datum, not additional existence assertions. The restriction-to-sections transport is obtained directly from the recorded restriction/evaluation equality.
